arxiv-2208-01950.title: An upper bound on the nullity of signed graphs This work was supported by the National Nature Science Foundation of China (Nos.11871040).
arxiv-2208-01950.creator: Keming Liu Xiying Yuan
arxiv-2208-01950.description: Abstract Abstract: In this paper, an upper bound on the nullity of signed graphs in terms of the cyclomatic number and the number of pendant vertices is proved, and the corresponding extremal signed graphs are completely characterized. Keywords: Signed graph; cyclomatic number; pendant vertices; nullity. 1 Introduction All graphs considered in this paper are simple and finite.

arxiv-2304-00945.title: Canonical decompositions of 3-connected graphs
arxiv-2304-00945.creator: Johannes Carmesin
arxiv-2304-00945.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Johannes Carmesin. We offer a new structural basis for the theory of 3-connected graphs, providing a unique decomposition of every such graph into parts that are either quasi 4-connected, wheels, or thickened K_{3,m} ’s. Our construction is explicit, canonical, and has the following applications: we obtain a new theorem characterising all Cayley graphs as either essentially 4-connected, cycles, or complete graphs on at most four vertices, and we provide an automatic proof of Tutte’s wheel theorem. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification.

arxiv-2402-03695.title: ConUNETR: A conditional transformer Network for 3D Micro-CT Embryonic Cartilage Segmentation
arxiv-2402-03695.creator: Nishchal Sapkota, Yejia Zhang, Susan M. Motch Perrine, Yuhan Hsi, Sirui Li, Meng Wu
arxiv-2402-03695.description: Abstract Studying the morphological development of cartilaginous and osseous structures is critical to the early detection of life-threatening skeletal dysmorphology. Embryonic cartilage undergoes rapid structural changes within hours, introducing biological variations and morphological shifts that limit the generalization of deep learning-based segmentation models that infer across multiple embryonic age groups.

arxiv-2501-05800.title: Quantum Berezinian for the Twisted Super Yangian
arxiv-2501-05800.creator: Hongda Lin Yongjie Wang, Honglian Zhang
arxiv-2501-05800.description: Abstract Motivated by an open problem proposed in Molev’s book [ 28 , Section 2.16, Example 16] , we investigate the quantum Berezinian 𝔅 t ​ w ​ ( u ) \mathfrak{B}^{tw}(u) associated with the twisted super Yangian, which is a coideal sub-superalgebra of the super Yangian of the general linear Lie superalgebra.

arxiv-2503-22063.title: Arch-VQ: Discrete Architecture Representation Learning with Autoregressive Priors
arxiv-2503-22063.creator: Deshani Geethika Poddenige, Sachith Seneviratne Asela Hevapathige, Damith Senanayake, Mahesan Niranjan, PN Suganthan, Saman Halgamuge (✉)
arxiv-2503-22063.description: Abstract Existing neural architecture representation learning methods focus on continuous representation learning, typically using Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) to map discrete architectures onto a continuous Gaussian distribution. However, sampling from these spaces often leads to a high percentage of invalid or duplicate neural architectures, likely due to the unnatural mapping of inherently discrete architectural space onto a continuous space.

arxiv-2503-23231.title: CCCI: Code Completion with Contextual Information for Complex Data Transfer Tasks Using Large Language Models
arxiv-2503-23231.creator: Hangzhan Jin, Mohammad Hamdaqa
arxiv-2503-23231.description: Abstract Unlike code generation, which involves creating code from scratch, code completion focuses on integrating new lines or blocks of code into an existing codebase. This process requires a deep understanding of the surrounding context, such as variable scope, object models, API calls, and database relations, to produce accurate results.

arxiv-2505-12017.title: Global regularity and decay estimates for the relativistic Landau equation Thanks: CH was supported by NSF grants DMS-2204615 and DMS-2337666. SS was supported by NSF grant DMS-213407. AT was supported by NSF grants DMS-2012333 and DMS-2408163. MT was supported by NSF grant DMS-2206187
arxiv-2505-12017.creator: Christopher Henderson, Stanley Snelson, Andrei Tarfulea, Maja Tasković
arxiv-2505-12017.description: Abstract . We consider the relativistic Landau equation in the spatially inhomogeneous, far-from-equilibrium regime. We establish regularity estimates of all orders, implying that solutions remain smooth for as long as some zeroth-order conditional bounds hold. We also prove that polynomial and exponential decay in the momentum variable is propagated forward in time.

arxiv-2510-22290.title: Analyzing GW231109_235456 and understanding its potential implications for population studies, nuclear physics, and multi-messenger astronomy
arxiv-2510-22290.creator: Thibeau Wouters, Anna Puecher, Peter T. H. Pang, Tim Dietrich
arxiv-2510-22290.description: Abstract We study the gravitational-wave trigger GW231109_235456, a sub-threshold binary neutron star merger candidate observed in the first part of the fourth observing run of the LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA collaboration. Assuming the trigger is of astrophysical origin, we analyze it using state-of-the-art waveform models and investigate the robustness of the inferred source parameters under different prior choices in Bayesian inference.

arxiv-2602-04195.title: Semantic Consensus Decoding: Backdoor Defense for Verilog Code Generation
arxiv-2602-04195.creator: Guang Yang, Xing Hu 1, Xiang Chen, Xin Xia
arxiv-2602-04195.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) for Verilog code generation are increasingly adopted in hardware design, yet remain vulnerable to backdoor attacks where adversaries inject malicious triggers during training to induce vulnerable hardware designs. Unlike patchable software vulnerabilities, hardware trojans become irreversible once fabricated, making remediation extremely costly or impossible.

pmc-10531325.creator: Christophe Le Clorennec, Karen Lee, Yuchen Huo, Peter E Zage, Elena Levantini
pmc-10531325.description: Neuroblastoma (NB) is a pediatric malignancy originating from neural crest cells of the sympathetic nervous system that accounts for 15% of all pediatric cancer deaths. Despite advances in treatment, high-risk NB remains difficult to cure, highlighting the need for novel therapeutic approaches.

pmc-11337698.title: Care coordination models for transition and long-term follow-up among childhood cancer survivors: a scoping review
pmc-11337698.creator: Cho Lee Wong, Carmen Wing Han Chan, Mengyue Zhang, Yin Ting Cheung, Ka Ming Chow, Chi Kong Li, William H C Li, Eden Brauer, Yongfeng Chen
pmc-11337698.description: AbstractObjectivesChildhood cancer survivors may experience complex health issues during transition and long-term follow-up (LTFU); therefore, high-quality healthcare is warranted. Care coordination is one of the essential concepts in advanced healthcare. Care coordination models vary among childhood cancer survivors in transition and LTFU.

pmc-11420251.title: Enhanced heterologous gene expression in Trichoderma reesei by promoting multicopy integration
pmc-11420251.creator: Hugues Mathis, Delphine Naquin, Antoine Margeot, Frederique Bidard
pmc-11420251.description: AbstractTrichoderma reesei displays a high capability to produce extracellular proteins and therefore is used as a platform for the expression of heterologous genes. In a previous study, an expression cassette with the constitutive tef1 promoter and the cbh1 terminator compatible with flow cytometry analysis was developed.

pmc-11507066.title: Anomalous Non-Hermitian Open-Boundary Spectrum
pmc-11507066.creator: Xi-Xi Bao, Gang-Feng Guo, Lei Tan, Wu-Ming Liu
pmc-11507066.description: For a long time, it was presumed that continuum bands could be readily encompassed by open-boundary spectra, irrespective of the system’s modest dimensions. However, our findings reveal a nuanced picture: under open-boundary conditions, the proliferation of complex eigenvalues progresses in a sluggish, oscillating manner as the system expands.

pmc-13633578.title: Parathyroid Carcinoma: A Report of Two Cases
pmc-13633578.creator: Cyrilkumaar Vijayakumar, Archit Dhanasekar, Ganapathy Dhanasekar
pmc-13633578.description: Parathyroid carcinoma is a rare cause of hypercalcaemia, which can be potentially difficult to diagnose and treat. Since its clinical, biochemical, and radiological features overlap with those of parathyroid adenoma, diagnosis is often made only after histological review of the resected tissue. We report two cases managed at a United Kingdom district general hospital.
